node.title: Re^2: Using 'no warnings' to disable own debug warn(ing)s?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Well, my thinking was that since I've used [doc://warnings::register] in my modules and warnings::warnif to create custom warnings, and that function is sensitive to FATAL warnings, I thought it'd be sensitive to no warnings as well, since AFAIK [doc://warn] just unconditionally warns (and AFAIK the only way to catch it is with [doc://%SIG]). And it does indeed work, but unfortunately it seems that it only works across package boundaries, I'm not entirely sure yet why, but from a quick look at the [https://perl5.git.perl.org/perl.git/blob/v5.26.2:/lib/warnings.pm#l344|source] it seems to be because it uses (parts of) [doc://Carp] under the hood, looking up the call stack.

use warnings; use strict; { package Foo; use warnings::register; sub bar { warnings::warnif("bar: $_[0]"); } } { no warnings; Foo::bar("inside"); } Foo::bar("outside"); use warnings::register; use Carp; { no warnings; warn "warn"; warnings::warn("warnings::warn"); carp "carp"; warnings::warnif("inside 2"); } warnings::warnif("outside 2"); __END__ bar: outside at w.pl line 17. warn at w.pl line 23. warnings::warn at w.pl line 24. carp at w.pl line 25.

So at the moment my only two suggestions are to either go across package boundaries like I did in the above, or write your own debug function, which I tend to do. Just one example from [https://bitbucket.org/haukex/hgpstools/src/ef4d857c61cf6142efda6d347afcdb7f56c61ac1/SerialPort.pm#SerialPort.pm-116|here]:

sub _debug { my ($self, $lvl, @out) = @_; return if $self->{debug}<$lvl || !@out; print STDERR __PACKAGE__, " DEBUG: ", @out, "\n"; } # ... $self->_debug(2, ...);
